This is an excellent opportunity to join an established accountancy practice in Edinburgh in a varied role, supporting a diverse portfolio of clients across payroll and CIS.

title: Legal Administrator
description:
Legal Administrator - Land and Rural

Location: Edinburgh
Job Type: Permanent, Full-Time

The Opportunity

An established professional services organisation is seeking a highly organised and proactive Legal Administrator to join its specialist property and rural affairs team based in Edinburgh.

This role offers an excellent opportunity to become part of a busy and supportive legal environment, providing comprehensive administrative support across a varied caseload involving property transactions, estate matters, leasing arrangements, renewable energy projects, and other land-related work.

Key Responsibilities

Client Onboarding & Compliance
- Support the onboarding of new clients and matters.
- Prepare engagement documentation and client care correspondence.
- Assist with Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Client (KYC) requirements.
- Maintain accurate client records and compliance documentation.

Matter Administration
- Open and maintain client files using the firm's case management systems.
- Prepare reports and update matter information as required.
- Ensure all documentation is recorded and managed accurately.
- Maintain electronic and manual filing systems.

Transactional & Property Support
- Request and prepare property searches and related documentation.
- Assist with registration documentation and submissions.
- Prepare Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (LBTT) returns and associated paperwork.
- Provide administrative support throughout property and land transactions.

Document Production
- Produce professional correspondence, reports, forms and legal documents.
- Format, proofread and edit documentation to a high standard.
- Undertake audio typing and dictation where required.
- Prepare presentations, meeting materials and supporting documentation.

Team Support
- Coordinate diary management and scheduling of appointments.
- Arrange travel and accommodation where required.
- Liaise professionally with clients, external contacts and internal stakeholders.
- Assist with the review and continuous improvement of departmental processes and procedures.
- Provide general administrative support to the wider team.

Person Specification

Essential Experience & Skills
- Previous experience in an administrative role within a legal, professional services or corporate environment.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work to deadlines.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Experience producing and editing professional documents.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
- Professional and client-focused approach.

Desirable Experience
- Previous experience within a legal administration or legal secretary role.
- Experience supporting property, conveyancing or rural business matters.
- Familiarity with case management systems.
- Understanding of AML and client onboarding processes.

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary and benefits package.
- Opportunity to work within a well-established and respected professional services environment.
- Structured training and development opportunities.
- Supportive team culture.
- Long-term career progression prospects.

title: Medical Records Administrator
description:

As a Medical Administrator, you'll play a key role in supporting safe, efficient care by managing and maintaining accurate medical records. In this role, you'll take responsibility for the preparation, tracking, and secure storage of medical records across outpatient, pre-assessment, and admissions clinics. You'll ensure records are organised, accurate, and accessible, responding promptly to requests while maintaining strict confidentiality in line with data protection requirements. From filing reports and correspondence to transporting records across departments, your attention to detail and organisation will be essential in a busy healthcare environment. This is a physically active role which involves regular movement around the hospital, handling large volumes of medical records, lifting and carrying files, and being on your feet for extended periods. Candidates should be comfortable undertaking these duties as part of their day-to-day responsibilities.

- Preparing and tracking patient records for outpatient, pre-assessment, and admissions clinics
- Organising, filing, and securely storing medical records, including archiving
- Responding promptly to requests for records and information
- Managing data input accurately and efficiently
- Handling general administrative duties such as telephone enquiries and photocopying
- Transporting records between departments as required
- Maintaining strict compliance with data protection regulation

Who we're looking for:
- Experience in a healthcare administration or medical records environment (desirable)
- Strong organisational skills and ability to manage priorities in a busy setting
- Confident using Microsoft Office and IT systems
- Excellent communication skills and a collaborative mindset
- Comfortable undertaking the physical aspects of the role, including frequent walking throughout the hospital, moving and transporting medical records, lifting and carrying files, and periods of standing

Working Hours: Full Time 37.5 hours per week Opening hours are 7am -8pm Monday to Friday
Saturday 7-3
Sunday 8-4
1 in 4 weekends
Contract Type: Permanent

Benefits:

We offer employees a competitive salary as well as a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your wellbeing, both inside and outside of work. This includes:
- 35 days' annual leave inclusive of bank holidays (pro rata) - helping you maintain a healthy work-life balance
- Access to private healthcare and health insurance options - giving you reassurance and faster access to care
- Gym and wellbeing benefits - supporting your physical and mental wellbeing
- Free on-site parking - making your day-to-day easier
- A supportive team within a leading independent healthcare provider - where you'll feel valued and part of something meaningful
- Employer and employee contributory pension with flexible retirement options - supporting your future
- 'Spire for you' reward platform - discount and cashback for over 1000 retailers
- Free Bupa wellness screening - helping you stay on top of your health

Our Values:

We are extremely proud of our heritage in private healthcare and of our values as an organisation:
- Driving clinical excellence
- Doing the right thing
- Caring is our passion.
- Keeping it simple
- Delivering on our promises
- Succeeding and celebrating together

We commit to our employees' well-being through work life balance, on-going development, support and reward.

"Spire Healthcare is a leading independent healthcare group in the United Kingdom, running 38 hospitals and over 50 clinics across England, Wales and Scotland. It provides diagnostics, inpatient, day case and outpatient care, operates a network of private GPs and provides workplace health services to over 800 corporate clients. Three Bridges Recruitment are delighted to partner with a prominent, rapidly growing UK professional services and legal group to appoint a Credit Controller based in Edinburgh. Following a period of strategic merger and expansion, this newly created role offers an ambitious credit professional the chance to take real ownership of an Edinburgh-focused ledger. Working as part of a collaborative, Scotland-wide finance team, you will act as a trusted advisor to Partners and departmental leaders, playing an instrumental role in optimising cash collection and driving down DSO across high-value matters.

Why Work Here?
- Competitive Package: Salary up to £32,000, future performance related bonus, 7% employer pension contribution, private healthcare, and option to purchase additional annual leave.
- Edinburgh Focus with Hybrid Flexibility: A collaborative office base in central Edinburgh with flexible hybrid working (following an initial onboarding period) and occasional travel to Glasgow when required.
- Genuine Autonomy & Influence: Collaborative ledger reviews with partners where you are empowered to challenge senior stakeholders when appropriate, advise on risk, and set collection strategy.
- Expanding, Dynamic Brand: Be part of a forward-thinking group integrating established legal brands, offering genuine career development and long-term stability.

About The Role?

Reporting to the Credit Control Manager and working closely with local stakeholders in Edinburgh, you will take full charge of day-to-day credit management and working capital optimisation:
- Ledger Ownership: Manage an allocated debtor ledger across diverse, high-value client accounts, proactively securing timely cash collections.
- Partner Engagement: Conduct structured, regular ledger reviews directly with Partners and Senior Associates, establishing agreed action plans and tailored recovery strategies.
- Stakeholder & Client Relations: Act as a brand ambassador, navigating sensitive or complex discussions with clients and tailoring your approach to preserve long-term commercial relationships.
- Query & Dispute Resolution: Investigate billing discrepancies and legacy aged-debt matters end-to-end, liaising with internal legal teams to unblock payments.
- DSO & Performance Management: Track and report on key credit metrics, contributing to ambitious group targets to reduce debtor days and mitigate bad debt risk.
- Process Improvement: Actively identify efficiencies across systems, billing flows, and collection processes within an integrating business.

About You?

We are looking for a commercially minded, resilient credit professional with a strong personality who can combine ledger competence with strong interpersonal skills:
- Experience: Proven track record in credit control, collections, or accounts receivable. Experience within legal, accountancy, or wider professional services is advantageous, though strong commercial B2 B backgrounds are welcomed.
- Communication & Backbone: Confident dealing with senior stakeholders and Partners; comfortable challenging constructively, negotiating tactfully, and holding firm on credit policy.
- Analytical & Organised: Skilled in ledger reconciliations, dispute resolution, and managing multi-matter billing structures with high attention to detail.
- Adaptable Approach: Ability to adjust communication style across diverse client sectors and handle sensitive accounts with discretion and diplomacy.

Apply

At Three Bridges Recruitment, two of our core values are "striving for brilliance" and "relatability." We want every applicant to have an excellent experience and ensure this opportunity genuinely aligns with your personal and professional ambitions.

If this role sounds like the right next step in your career, please apply with your CV or contact Ryan Strachan at Three Bridges Recruitment for a confidential discussion.
